keptItems.title: The Lights Are Back On in Gary, Indiana
keptItems.summaryEvidence: Last night, NIPSCO, an Indiana utility company that provides electricity to half a million people in the northern part of the state, finally made the deadline for restoring power to the city of Gary. On August 11, a derecho swept across northwest Indiana, and winds nearing 100 miles an hour knocked out power for more than 370,000 people, NIPSCO has said. In Gary, home to nearly 70,000 people, 75 percent of them Black, more than half of the utility’s customers lost power in the initial aftermath of the storm. For the next two weeks, NIPSCO kept pushing back its timeline for restoring power; even on Monday, thousands in Gary were still in the dark. As of yesterday evening, the utility said, it had restored power to 99 percent of its customers—which also meant that hundreds of people in Gary still didn’t have electricity this morning. Blackouts follow plenty of storms, and at a press conference eight days after the storm hit, Gary Mayor Eddie Melton described the ongoing blackout as a situation for “not just Gary” but also all of northwest Indiana. However, as the days of darkness stretched on, and the power started going back in other parts of the region—first Dyer and East Chicago, then Hobart and Merrillville—the initial inconvenience of a Tuesday, a Wednesday, then a Thursday, then a Friday without power started to become a crisis in Gary. This past weekend, Melton was no longer talking about the blackout as a regional problem. Gary, he told me, had not initially been on NIPSCO’s schedule for restoring power and had seemingly been overlooked until the city pushed back. NIP

keptItems.title: What Are Jewish Voters Supposed to Do?
keptItems.summaryEvidence: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube On this week’s episode of The David Frum Show , The Atlantic ’s David Frum opens with his thoughts on the blowing up of trade talks between the United States and Canada, and President Trump’s reckless trade war against Canada. David discusses how this trade war hurts not only America’s relationship with Canada but its global standing as a reliable trade partner. Then David is joined by Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel to discuss the growing hostility among some Democratic voters toward American Jews. Frum and Nessel discuss why the rhetoric of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed concerns some Jews; rise of anti-Semitism within the Democratic party; and the impossible situation many Jewish voters find themselves in today. Finally, David ends the show with his thoughts on the new biography on Roy Cohn, American Scoundrel . The following is a transcript of the episode: Dana Nessel: I think it’s a fundamental mistake for the Democratic Party to think that you can just push Jewish Democrats out and simply replace them with any other population.
